title: Efficient Weighted Graph Matching on GPUs
problem: Weighted graph matching on GPUs faces challenges from irregular memory access patterns, load imbalances, and massive graph sizes exceeding available GPU memory. Multi-GPU systems introduce additional complexities from data dependencies and device synchronization costs.
motivation: Weighted matching is fundamental to applications in linear algebra, multi-level graph algorithms, computer vision, and machine learning, making efficient implementations critical.
method: The algorithm works by having each point in the graph greedily select its best-weighted neighbor as a match, using pointers to track these pairs. The computation is then distributed across multiple NVIDIA A100 and V100 GPUs on DGX systems, with the graph broken into batches. Graph matching normally causes two problems: unpredictable memory access patterns and frequent synchronization (waiting) between GPUs. The paper solves this by strategically assigning graph batches to different GPUs to reduce these bottlenecks.
key_novelty: The core innovation is pairing a locally greedy matching algorithm with multi-GPU batching and distribution strategies to efficiently handle graphs larger than a single GPU's memory.
contributions: Efficient approximation algorithms for locally dominant weighted graph matching
Multi-GPU batching and distribution strategy for massive graph processing
2-45× performance improvement over state-of-the-art single-GPU and CPU implementations
Analysis of GPU data distribution considerations for practical weighted matching
primary_theme: GPU-accelerated weighted matching via multi-GPU distribution
